question: A 64-year-old postmenopausal woman (not on HRT) presents with a single episode of vaginal spotting. Transvaginal ultrasound shows endometrial thickness of 6 mm. What is the MOST appropriate next step?

answers.text: Reassure and discharge — a single episode of spotting is usually benign atrophy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Reassurance without investigation is NEVER appropriate for PMB. The cardinal rule is that endometrial carcinoma must be excluded in every case.

answers.text: Repeat TVS in 6 months and treat empirically with vaginal oestrogen

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Delayed investigation is inappropriate. An endometrial thickness of ≥4 mm in a postmenopausal woman not on HRT mandates tissue sampling.

answers.text: Endometrial sampling (outpatient pipelle biopsy or hysteroscopy with biopsy)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The threshold for endometrial sampling in a postmenopausal woman NOT on HRT is an endometrial thickness ≥4 mm on TVS. At 6 mm, tissue sampling is mandatory to exclude endometrial carcinoma.

answers.text: CT scan of abdomen and pelvis for staging

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Staging investigations are ordered AFTER a tissue diagnosis of carcinoma is confirmed. CT cannot replace histopathological diagnosis.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the rule: TVS endometrial thickness ≥4 mm (not on HRT) or ≥8 mm (on HRT) requires endometrial sampling. This patient has 6 mm — tissue diagnosis is mandatory.
Well done. The TVS cut-off for endometrial sampling in postmenopausal women NOT on HRT is ≥4 mm. At 6 mm, endometrial biopsy is mandatory.
